# Project agent rules

This file is the baseline set of rules for agents working in this repository. All agents must follow it in addition to any project-specific instructions found in parent directories.

## Core rules

- Respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in code, comments, or documentation.
- Never use the em-dash character in any text, code, comment, or content. Use a comma, period, colon, or parentheses instead.
- Keep changes consistent with the structure, naming, and style of the surrounding code.
- Treat unfamiliar files and changes as potential user work. Investigate before deleting or overwriting them.
- Do not question or doubt whether the user has already performed an action such as a deploy, commit, or send.

## Working in this codebase

- Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands. Fall back to the shell only when a tool cannot do what is needed.
- Use the write tool to create or replace files, and the edit tool for targeted changes to existing text files.
- Fix all diagnostics in files you edit, not just the ones you introduced.
- Preserve existing code comments when editing files. Do not delete or rewrite them during refactors.
- Keep files focused and avoid unnecessary duplication. Extract repeated snippets into shared helpers when the same pattern appears in three or more places.

## Testing and verification

- When the repository has a test runner configured, add or update tests for every behavior change.
- Run the test suite before declaring work complete. In this Go workspace, use `go test ./...`.
- Verify changes with the smallest command that proves the behavior, then run the full suite.

## Commits

- Write commit messages in English by default.
- Keep conventional-commit prefixes such as `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `style:`, and `refactor:` unchanged.
- Check the repository history before choosing a different language for commit messages.

## Scope

- Assume the local environment only. Never access, deploy to, or assume a production environment.
- Do not create new credentials when a reusable one already exists. Read the relevant documentation before handling secrets.
- Never print or commit secret values.
